_comment: Group 2 of 3: changes reach the default branch through a pull request, and a PR
with open review threads cannot merge.
required_review_thread_resolution is TRUE, and it is what actually prevents a merge
over open findings: both review bots submit as COMMENTED, so reviewDecision stays
clean however many threads are unresolved.
required_approving_review_count is 0 because GitHub does not let a PR author approve
their own PR -- 1 makes every solo PR unmergeable (tinbee/web PRs #2 and #3).
There is deliberately NO copilot_code_review rule, here or in any group. That rule
makes Copilot review automatically -- on every PR when it opens, and on every push
with review_on_push -- which is how a four-push PR collected five reviews and hit the
account rate limit (tinbee/foliot#15, 2026-09-29). Copilot reviews only when asked:
add the `copilot-review` label and copilot-review.yml requests it, the same shape as
claude-review. By hand that is:
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N/requested_reviewers -X POST \
-f 'reviewers[]=copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]'
The [bot] suffix is required -- without it the API answers 422 'Reviews may only be
requested from collaborators', which makes it look impossible. requested_reviewers
reads empty straight afterwards because Copilot consumes the request rather than
queueing it, so a new review appearing is the only confirmation.
Every parameter GitHub echoes back is spelled out, defaults included, so that a
byte-for-byte comparison with the live ruleset is meaningful.
./rulesets/apply.sh [--check] pr-flow <owner/repo>
name: pr-flow
